Nicknamed "'''Crash'''", he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] and voted to the [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]] while with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in 2010. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. == High school and college career == Wallace attended Childersburg High School in [[Childersburg, Alabama]], where he had a very successful career. For his senior season efforts, he was named the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]], an honor given to the best high school basketball player.[https://www.espn.com/ncb/s/2000/1101/850675.html] Wallace attended the [[University of Alabama]] for one season before declaring himself eligible for the [[2001 NBA draft]]. Wallace was drafted in the first round as the 25th overall pick.{{Cite web |title=NBA Draft 2001 |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2001/draft_board.html?nav=TextNavBar |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205155018/http://www.nba.com/draft2001/draft_board.html?nav=TextNavBar |archive-date=February 5, 2012 |access-date=August 2, 2018 |website=www.nba.com}} In 2000–01, he averaged 9.8 points and 6.0 rebounds per game. ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2001–2004)=== In three seasons with the [[Sacramento Kings]], Wallace rarely played, but in his brief appearances, he made himself known for his versatility and extraordinary athleticism. In the 2002 [[Slam Dunk Contest]], Wallace finished second to two-time winner [[Jason Richardson]]. On December 1, 2002, Wallace led Sacramento in scoring with a then-career-high 21 points, and grabbed eight rebounds, during a 103–84 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20230602001519/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/221201023 Kings defeat Rockets for ninth straight time] During his tenure with the Kings, Wallace was the odd man out in a deep roster that included All-Stars [[Chris Webber]], [[Peja Stojaković]], and [[Vlade Divac]]. ===Charlotte Bobcats (2004–2011)=== Wallace was selected by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] as part of the [[2004 NBA expansion draft]].{{Cite basketball-reference|name=Gerald Wallace|id=w/wallage01|date=November 28, 2015}} In his first season he averaged 11.1 points, 5.5 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 1.3 blocks a game. He continued to improve in 2005–06, before getting injured in January, averaging 14.5 points and 7 rebounds, and ranking in the top 10 in the NBA in field goal percentage (54.142), blocks (2.19), and steals per game (2.44). Since the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] began counting blocks as a statistic in 1973, only two other players ([[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] and [[Hakeem Olajuwon]]) in league history have averaged over 2.0 blocks and 2.0 steals per game in a single season. Wallace was known for his somewhat reckless style of play that led to frequent injuries and earned him the nickname "Crash".{{Cite web |date=February 26, 2008 |title=Bobcats reach out to NFL's Panthers for help with Wallace's concussion |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3265951 |access-date=February 26, 2008 |publisher=ESPN}} He missed a total of 39 games in his first two years with the [[Charlotte Hornets|Bobcats]], but his energetic and sometimes dangerous behavior that may have caused his injuries was also what contributed to his gaudy defensive stats. Coach [[Bernie Bickerstaff]] said of Wallace, "Gerald can only play one way and be effective. Energy – that's his game." In 2006, Wallace attempted to refine his game in order to avoid being injured, and as a result his numbers suffered. The first month of the season, Wallace had only five total blocks (an average of .3 per game) and his averages were down across the stat line from 2005. Wallace improved his play in the second month of the season, but he went down with a [[separated shoulder]] in a December game against the [[Indiana Pacers]]. When he returned, Wallace continued his fine play finishing the season averaging 18.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2 steals, and 1 block in 72 games. [[Image:Rip Shoots.jpg|thumb|240px|right|Wallace contesting [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]]'s jump shot in January 2009]] Wallace appeared opposite [[Tim Duncan]] in the March 2008 "SLAM-UP" centerfold for ''[[SLAM Magazine]]''. Wallace suffered a Grade 3 [[concussion]] on February 23, 2008, after taking an unintentional elbow to the face from Sacramento's [[Mikki Moore]]. It was his fourth concussion in as many seasons with the Bobcats. It was not clear when he would return, although Grade 3 concussions are defined by the [[American Association of Neurological Surgeons]] as ones that "involve post-traumatic amnesia for more than 24 hours or unconsciousness for more than five minutes. Players who sustain this grade of brain injury should be sidelined for at least one month, after which they can return to play if they are asymptomatic for one week."{{Cite web |date=February 29, 2008 |title=Occupational Hazard: Updates on Yao, Butler, G. Wallace |url=https://www.espn.com/fantasy/basketball/fba/story?page=nbainjury0229 |access-date=February 29, 2008 |publisher=ESPN}} He returned later on in the season, finishing the year with a new career high in points, assists, and minutes. He suffered a partially [[pneumothorax|collapsed lung]] and a [[fractured rib]] after being [[flagrant foul|flagrantly fouled]] while driving for a layup by [[Los Angeles Lakers]]' [[Andrew Bynum]] on January 27, 2009, and was forced to miss seven games. He also was unable to fly and instead crossed the United States en route back to Charlotte by bus.{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2009 |title=Wallace injured in collision with Bynum |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3866849 |access-date=January 28, 2009 |publisher=ESPN}} Wallace was selected to play in the [[2010 NBA All-Star Game]] in Dallas,{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2010 |title=Gerald Wallace All-Star profile |url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2010/players/gerald_wallace.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100523162725/http://www.nba.com/allstar2010/players/gerald_wallace.html |archive-date=May 23, 2010 |access-date=April 12, 2010 |website=NBA.com}} becoming the first and only Charlotte Bobcat to do so (with the Bobcats changing their name back to their original Hornets name after reclaiming the Charlotte NBA history originally owned by the [[New Orleans Hornets|Pelicans]] franchise in 2014). Wallace was also selected to participate in the 2010 [[NBA All-Star Weekend Slam Dunk Contest]]. He was also selected to the 2010–2012 [[USA Basketball]] Men's National Team to represent the United States in the 2010 [[FIBA World Championship]] along with a possible trip with the team to the 2012 Olympics.{{Cite web |date=February 13, 2010 |title=Gerald Wallace named to USA national team |url=http://blog.al.com/kevin-scarbinsky/2010/02/gerald_wallace_named_to_usa_na.html |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=AL.com}} In the first-ever playoff game for the Bobcats, Wallace led the team with 25 points. This franchise playoff single game scoring record lasted until game 2 of the series, when [[Stephen Jackson]] broke the record by scoring 27 points. In 2010, Wallace was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team.{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2010 |title=Orlando's Howard, Boston's Rondo lead All-Defensive Team |url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/05/all.defense/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100508064557/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/05/05/all.defense/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt2 |archive-date=May 8, 2010 |access-date=May 5, 2010 |website=NBA.com}} During the 2010–2011 season as a Bobcat, he averaged 15.6 points per game, 8.2 rebounds per game, and 2.4 assists per game in 39 minutes per game. He played 48 games with the team during the season. Wallace is one of three players in NBA history (the others being [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] and [[Hakeem Olajuwon]]) to average at least two steals and two blocks per game over the course of an entire season. ===Portland Trail Blazers (2011–2012)=== On February 24, 2011, Wallace was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Joel Przybilla]], [[Dante Cunningham]], [[Sean Marks]], and two future draft picks.{{Cite press release |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Gerald Wallace |date=February 24, 2011 |publisher=Portland Trail Blazers |url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/120/ItemID/2324/Default.aspx |access-date=February 24, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302201136/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/120/ItemID/2324/Default.aspx |archive-date=March 2, 2011 |url-status=usurped}} He provided help for the team while [[Brandon Roy]] was injured. The Trail Blazers finished 48–34, good for the playoffs. They lost in the opening round to the Dallas Mavericks in 6 games. In the next season as a Trail Blazer, Wallace averaged 13.3 points per game, 6.6 rebounds per game, and 2.7 assists per game in 35.8 minutes per game. He played 42 games with the team that season. ===New Jersey/Brooklyn Nets (2012–2013)=== [[File:Gerald Wallace Nets.jpg|thumb|170px|right|Wallace with the Nets in March 2013]] On March 15, 2012, Wallace was traded from the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] to the [[New Jersey Nets]] in exchange for [[Shawne Williams]], [[Mehmet Okur]] and a 2012 top-3 protected 1st round draft pick (which became [[Damian Lillard]]).{{Cite web |last=Marc Stein |date=March 16, 2012 |title=Nets agree to acquire Gerald Wallace |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/7690823/new-jersey-nets-making-run-portland-trail-blazers-gerald-wallace-sources-say |access-date=March 16, 2012 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On April 8, 2012, Wallace injured his left leg on a put back dunk and played only two more games that season.{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2012 |title=Gerald Wallace soars for huge put-back dunk, injures left leg on the landing (VIDEO) |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/gerald-wallace-soars-huge-put-back-dunk-injures-173459714.html |access-date=April 9, 2012 |website=yahoo.com |publisher=yahoo}} Wallace played in 16 total games for the Nets that season and averaged 15.2 points per game. On July 11, 2012, Wallace re-signed with the Nets. The contract was reportedly worth $40 million for four years.{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2012 |title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Gerald Wallace |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Wallace_Signing_Release_120711.html |access-date=July 11, 2012 |website=NBA.com}} In the first game of the season Wallace injured his left ankle. With just 27 seconds left on the game clock, Wallace got hurt trying to block a shot by Raptors point guard [[Kyle Lowry]]. After the game the team announced it was a sprained left ankle. Wallace missed six games before making his return.{{Cite web |date=February 27, 2013 |title=Gerald Wallace playing through pain for Brooklyn Nets, admits to physical and mental slump |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/nets-wallace-admits-physical-mental-slump-article-1.1275554 |access-date=February 27, 2013 |website=New York Daily News |publisher=nydailynews.com}} Wallace got injured again when the Nets played the [[Phoenix Suns]] on January 11, 2013. Wallace injured his ribs after the Phoenix Suns player [[P. J. Tucker]] fouled him hard while attempting a fast break dunk early in the first quarter. Wallace landed awkwardly on the floor and remained on the court for several moments before being helped to get on his feet and to the locker room. He did not return to the game. Wallace missed two games.{{Cite web |last=Patt |first=Jason |date=January 12, 2013 |title=Gerald Wallace injury: Bruised ribs for Nets forward |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/1/12/3869124/gerald-wallace-injury-nets-ribs |access-date=January 12, 2013 |website=sbnation.com |publisher=sbnation}} ===Boston Celtics (2013–2015)=== Wallace was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] on July 12, 2013, in a multi-player deal that sent [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]], and [[Jason Terry]] to the Nets.{{Cite web |date=July 12, 2013 |title=Celtics Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-brooklyn-nets |access-date=July 12, 2013 |website=[[NBA.com]]}} On February 28, 2014, Wallace was ruled out for the rest of the season after an MRI revealed a torn meniscus in his left knee.{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2014 |title=Celtics Slammed With Laundry List of Injuries |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/celtics-slammed-laundry-list-injuries |access-date=March 1, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web |date=February 28, 2014 |title=Gerald Wallace's 2014 |website=CBSSports.com}} On July 27, 2015, Wallace was traded, along with [[Chris Babb]], to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]].{{Cite web |date=July 27, 2015 |title=Warriors Trade David Lee to Boston in Exchange for Gerald Wallace & Chris Babb |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-trade-david-lee-boston-exchange-gerald-wallace-chris-babb |access-date=July 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} Four days later, Wallace was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], along with cash and draft considerations, in exchange for [[Jason Thompson (basketball)|Jason Thompson]].{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2015 |title=Sixers Acquire Gerald Wallace And A Draft Consideration |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150731-trade |access-date=July 31, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On September 27, 2015, he was waived by the 76ers.{{Cite web |date=September 27, 2015 |title=SIXERS ANNOUNCE 2015 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2015-training-camp-roster |access-date=September 27, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} Wallace's final NBA game was Game 4 of the 2015 Eastern Conference First Round on April 26, 2015, against the Cleveland Cavaliers. Boston lost the game 93 – 101 with Wallace recording 1 rebound and no other stats in 3 and half minutes of playing time. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===Regular
